new_findings.title: Reader concurrency test can fail solely because the writer finishes first
new_findings.trigger: The scheduler runs the writer through all twelve commits before the parent reaches its first while-condition, or permits the reader only Busy observations until the writer finishes.
new_findings.impact: The final observed > 0 assertion fails even when every commit and observation is coherent, making a purported deterministic local gate scheduler-dependent.
new_findings.evidence: The writer has no handshake with the reader; the parent reads only while !writer.is_finished() and then requires at least one successful Current observation. Joining the writer and checking final generation does not guarantee any loop iteration.
new_findings.reproduction: Static schedule analysis of lines 2777-2831; no executable reproduction or test execution performed.
new_findings.acceptance_relevance: Reliability of required deterministic semantic Gate A validation; not evidence of production state corruption.
new_findings.recommendation: Coordinate at least one reader observation with the writer using an explicit handshake, then assert coherent observations and final generation without depending on scheduler fairness.

limitations: No fresh tests, builds, remote effects, credential access or unsafe probes.
Older unchanged test body lines 36-1006 remains outside this added-module assignment.
